Latin word

caccabus

caccabus (cacabus), caccabī m.

noun, second declension

cooking pot

In this lexicon

  • cooking pot

    the recommended word · classical · M-O s.v. pan: pot (cacabus); Varro; Stat. Silv. 4.9.45

Notes

  1. 1caccabus: short a, double c (Lewis & Short cācabus, taking the heavy first syllable for a long vowel). Greek κάκκαβος. Varro writes caccabum (cited by Lewis & Short); Stat. Silv. 4.9.45, albōrum calicum atque caccabōrum, scans the first syllable heavy, as the double c makes it. Comenius’s cacabīs is marked the same way. Ruling: caccabus: a short a and a double c (provisional).

Examples

  • ēlixat ōllīs et cacabīs in focō

    he boils in pots and pans on the hearthComen. OP 54
